full_judgment:
45. As to the next contention of the learned Advocate for the convict appellant, that Abdul Jalil who is said to have opened the door of the hut, by removing the chain put by the accused Rehana, was a vital witness, but he was not adduced by the prosecution and accordingly the presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act is to be drawn in this case. But, having examined the FIR, the charge sheet, the examination made under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the judgment of the Court below we find that this Abdul Jalil Mollah is father of the accused Jamal and both of them live in two separate huts of the same homestead. This fact has been duly taken into notice by the tribunal as it appears from the judgment as the learned tribunal has also recorded its finding to the effect that, “কিন্তু স্বাক্ষী প্রদানে তাহার অনুপস্থিতির করাণ স্পষ্ট এবং পরিষ্কার।”We can safely assume that all these particulars and facts were noticed by the learned Counsel for the convict-appellant and instead of making submission on this point he either could have brought it to the notice of the Court, as he is duty bound as an officer of the Court or could have abstained from so strenuously pressing this as a ground for setting aside the conviction. 

 46. Besides, it is pertinent to note here that a presumption under section 114 of the Evidence Act, 1872 is merely a presumption of fact and it is not incumbent upon the Court to draw any presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, unless there is exist a compelling reason for that.
